A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CodeFlow and focal preference-alignment research despite the title and method renaming. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including v3's Appendices A-C; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training evaluations, ablations, debugging pass rates and generated-code error analyses in Tables 1-2 and Figures 3, 5 and 6.

after.justification: V3 retains original training results and adds original test-quality audits, controlled comparisons, sensitivity analyses and teacher-model experiments throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: IterPref becomes Target-DPO/Target-RPO, retaining iterative debugging, randomly selected failed-iteration negatives, LCS difference extraction and full-positive/masked-negative preference losses. The added audits and alternative-teacher experiments do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench task coverage is retained. V3 adds EpiCoder training-data comparisons and auxiliary dataset analysis involving Alpaca, CodeFeedback, Evol-Alpaca and OSS-Instruct (Tables 2 and 17), extending data coverage within the existing research focus.

E2.justification: V3 adds reported CodeDPO and PLUM comparisons (Figure 4; Table 12), EpiCoder-SFT comparisons, and vanilla DPO rows for StarCoder2-15B and Qwen2.5-Coder-7B in Table 1. The evaluated AceCoder comparison in v1 Figure 5 disappears, although its related-work mention remains.

E3.justification: V1 specifies two training epochs for instruction-tuned models and five for base models; v3 Appendix A.3 specifies three epochs and no longer documents validation-loss checkpoint selection. This is a reported protocol revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Added experiments also introduce model-size, training-volume, teacher-model and test-quality evaluation settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds debugging-versus-sampling controls, synthetic-test audits, correct-versus-incorrect SFT, hyperparameter and model-size analyses, LCS-versus-prefix/suffix extraction, negative-selection comparisons and alternative-teacher experiments. These substantially extend v1's SFT, context and masking ablations. The original error-frequency and annotation-cost analyses are retained in Appendices C.5-C.6.

E5.justification: V3 introduces sample-level dispersion summaries, including a coverage boxplot with mean and quintile markers and judge-score distribution summaries (Figures 7-8). These describe variability across sampled cases; neither version reports training-run seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive results for new comparisons, audits and ablations while retaining most headline scores. Table 1 revises Qwen2.5-Coder-7B/RPO's BigCodeBench-Hard Complete/Instruct scores from 24.3/14.8 to 14.2/13.5, and its average from 42.7 to 41.4. These are changed reported values, not established same-setting performance losses given the revised training description.

T1.justification: The LCS algorithm, preference-loss equations and reinforcement-learning objective are retained without substantive mathematical revision. V3's added code-coverage formula explains a standard evaluation metric; no new theorem, proof or formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain iterative-debugging preference construction, the CodeFlow dataset, targeted preference optimization and improved code-generation performance across models and benchmarks. The new emphasis on understanding code and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive arguments about the five-iteration cutoff, synthetic-test validity, dataset diversity, random-negative generalization and applicability across teacher models. V1's general warning about generated-test quality becomes a more specific appendix qualification that tests can be simple and miss edge cases; the dataset-size limitation remains.

D1.justification: V3 supplies generation and judging prompts, a generated-test example, coverage-evaluation tools, benchmark software versions, a 3% warm-up specification and separate prompt/generation limits. V1 promises future code/data release; v3 states that code, models and datasets are available through a supplied repository. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V3 adds Hu et al. (2025) on coarse-to-fine process rewards and removes Li et al. (2025) on gradient-based parameter selection. It also identifies CodeDPO as concurrent work and sharpens the contrast with pass-rate supervision, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and explanatory passages undergo substantial rewriting alongside the title and method renaming. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, and the main error/cost analyses move into the appendix, substantially reorganizing the narrative around experiments and ablations.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a bar chart to a radial comparison, and v3 adds an ablation diagram, test-quality displays and prompt/example figures. Existing ablation tables are restructured and expanded. V1's iteration plot is redrawn as v3 Figure 6, while its error-frequency chart is redisplayed as Table 18.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses v1's lack of direct synthetic-test audits and controlled evidence for LCS and random-negative selection through Appendix A.2 and C.7-C.8. Additional baselines and explicit synthesis prompts strengthen the evidential basis and reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, although corrections remain necessary: Qwen Target-RPO's LiveCodeBench score is 32.2 in Table 1 but 33.3 in Tables 9 and 16, and the changed training-epoch statement is unexplained.
